key_points.point: The authors propose a formal mechanism design framework to ensure AI regulation is enforceable and robust against strategic evasion by model providers. By framing regulation as a 'mechanism design problem under uncertainty,' they aim to create a system where providers must 'bet' their own capital on the safety of their models. This approach seeks to prevent catastrophic risks by ensuring that non-compliant models are effectively excluded from the market.
key_points.verbatim: In this work, we formalise this problem by casting AI regulation as a mechanism design problem under uncertainty. We propose regulation mechanisms which push the burden of proof on the providers. Instead of trying to prove ‘This model is unsafe’, the regulator now judges, ‘Is the model provider willing to bet their own capital on the model’s safety?’
